subject: FintechX POC - Observability & Success Criteria
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@fintechx.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, dev_patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Feb 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: FintechX POC - Observability & Success Criteria

Hi Sarah — great chat today, thanks for the time. Per our call, here’s a concise recap and proposed plan for the 2-week POC focused on observability and acceptance criteria. Please review and confirm owners/timelines.

POC objective (what success looks like)
- Latency: p95 generation latency <= 250ms for the low-latency route (50–75 token prompts) under 30 RPS synthetic load.
- Reliability: error rate < 0.5% (4xx/5xx) and no more than 1 production-impacting incident during the POC window.
- Quality: model responses pass your eval set with >= 90% correctness on the 150-sample test prompts you’ll share.
- Cost visibility: per-1000-token cost is tracked and within the budget threshold you shared (TBD final number).

Evaluation plan & timeline
- Prep (this week): exchange eval prompts and access details. Redwood to provision a dedicated trial environment.
- Run (2 weeks starting 2026-02-22): baseline run + stress window.
- Wrap (1 week): joint review, metrics handoff, recommended next steps.
Owners
- FintechX PM / acceptance owner: Sarah Liu (you)
- Redwood POC lead: Marissa Cole (me) — coordination + dashboard setup
- Redwood infra owner: Rishi Malhotra — provisioning, tracing, log export
- Redwood eng: Dev Patel — instrumentation and KM/log forwarding setup

Observability plan (must-haves for the POC)
1) Dashboards (we’ll provision a shared Redwood dashboard view):
   - Overview: p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate, requests/s, tokens/s, cost per 1k tokens
   - Per-route: latency and error trends for each API route (generate, chat, embeddings)
   - Model-level: model variant usage, fallback counts, quantization profile in use
   - Cache & throughput: KV cache hit ratio, cache evictions, request queue length, batch size distribution
   - Infra: GPU utilization, CPU, memory, and network egress by node pool
2) Tracing:
   - Distributed traces with request_id, route, model_variant, backend_latency, tokenization_time, and any downstream calls (e.g., logging, embedding calls)
   - Sampling: 1% baseline + 100% for error traces (configurable)
3) Logs & exports:
   - Structured request logs (no full response body storage unless agreed) with request_id, prompt hash, token counts, model variant, error stack if any
   - Error logs with stack and host tag for quick triage
   - Export options: push to your S3 bucket or to Datadog/Splunk — Redwood can send via secure transfer; retention configurable
4) Key metrics to monitor (alerts & dashboards)
   - p95 latency (generate/chat)
   - Error rate (% of requests with 4xx/5xx)
   - Token throughput (tokens/sec) and requests/sec
   - Cost per 1k tokens and per-session cost estimate
   - Model fallback events (count & reason)
   - KV cache hit ratio
   - Batch size distribution and queue length (backpressure indicators)
   - GPU utilization and memory pressure (to correlate infra throttles)

Data & security notes
- For the POC we will not persist full response bodies unless you explicitly opt in; tracing will include request metadata and prompt hashes only.
- We’ll provide a temporary API key scoped to the POC; if you want logs exported into your own cloud account we’ll need an S3 path or Datadog token.

Next steps (action items)
- Sarah: share eval prompt CSV + list of 3 representative production routes and the acceptance owner.
- FintechX: provide target budget per-1k-token if available.
- Rishi/Dev (Redwood): provision POC env, enable tracing and populate dashboards.
- Marissa: share the dashboard link + runbook (I’ll attach the initial observability dashboard PNG).

Attachments: POC-observability-dashboard.png (preview), sample eval prompt template (CSV)

Thanks — I’ll follow up with proposed calendar blocks for a kickoff on 2026-02-22.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise POC Lead | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0142

Thanks Marissa — this is great and aligns with what we discussed. A few confirmations from our side: 

- Timeline: 2026-02-22 start works; we expect a 2-week active run and 1 week for review.
- Success criteria: agree on latency and reliability targets above. For cost we’ll provide a threshold by EOD Thursday (finance needs to sign off).
- Owners: I’ll be the PM/acceptance owner. I’m looping in Carlos Mendez (infra lead) for AWS/S3 details.

I attached our eval prompts CSV (FintechX-eval-prompts.csv) — it includes 150 prompts across the three routes you mentioned. We also included a short list of test users and a set of golden answers for the quality checks.

For log export: we prefer S3 export to our secure bucket (will share the path + IAM details once Carlos is back online). We’ll need the temporary API key and an ingress IP allowlist for the trial environment.

Quick question on tracing: will Redwood include the model_variant in the trace/span metadata? That will be important for us to correlate fallbacks.

Thanks — I’ll confirm the budget threshold ASAP.

Best,
Sarah

sarah.liu@fintechx.com | +1 (212) 555-0199
